Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you confirm
you're comfortable continuing?
A: Yes, that's fine.
Q: Please describe in your own words what happened on the day of the accident.
A: I was driving on a two-lane road in Pearland, heading toward a shopping center. The traffic was light. A car coming
from the opposite direction drifted into my lane while making a turn, and we ended up in a head-on collision. It wasn't
a high-speed impact, but it was enough to push my car back a bit and jolt me forward.
Q: Were you able to get out of your vehicle at the scene?
A: Yes, I got out on my own. My neck and shoulder felt tight right away, but I didn't think much of it at first.
Q: Did you seek medical attention?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic later that same day. They checked my shoulder, took some X-rays, and told me
there was no fracture. They recommended rest and a sling for a few days.
Q: Have you had any follow-up treatment since then?
A: Yes, I started physical therapy about a week later. The shoulder still hurts when I lift anything above my head or
reach behind me, and I've had trouble sleeping on that side.
Q: Did you have any pain or problems with that shoulder before the collision?
A: No, I hadn't had any issues with it before. I'm active and I hadn't seen a doctor for it.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about the accident or your injuries?
A: Only that I'm still working through the therapy, and I'd appreciate a clear explanation of the next steps for my claim.
Q: Thank you. We'll follow up in writing with those details. That concludes our call.
A: Thank you.
</page>
